entries.behavior: Builds commits with Git plumbing on a private index and moves a ref only if it has not moved; reads files and trees of a commit.

simplification.attempt: A checkout of the evidence branch was rejected without trying it: it needs a second working tree and cannot be safe for overlapping writers.

performance.attempt: Files on disk are hashed by one git process instead of one per file; generated content still costs one process each. Not measured.

entries.behavior: Adds the source scanner behind the registry and the dependency graph (dea2a61): it masks comments and strings, finds blocks, exports, imports and parameters, measures size, nesting and complexity per block, resolves imports to files, and reads files from the working tree or from Git.

simplification.attempt: A text scanner over masked source was written instead of adding a compiler dependency for each language.

performance.attempt: Not benchmarked.

entries.behavior: Splits the module and Wasm adapters into a core that uses only web platform APIs and a Node subclass that adds file loading, and publishes the core as the edge entry; behaviour under Bun and Node is unchanged.

simplification.attempt: The adapter logic exists once in the base class instead of being copied for the edge; the Node classes shrank to their file handling.

performance.attempt: No call path changed; the Wasm instantiate goes through compile then instantiate, which was not measured.

entries.behavior: Adds the runtime contract and its targets (ab9d6a2): a unit can run in-process, as a one-shot or persistent JSON process, as core Wasm or behind loopback HTTP with the same typed envelope, deadlines and error codes, and declared targets are turned into working runtimes.

simplification.attempt: Every target implements one invoke contract, so callers do not branch on where a unit runs.

performance.attempt: Each target is timed by harness kernel bench; no optimisation of the adapters themselves was attempted.

entries.behavior: Stores and reads Git LFS objects by content hash in the shared object store and transfers them with a remote; no LFS filter is needed.

simplification.attempt: First version used one fixed temporary name per object; two writers of identical media collided, as the independent probe showed. Each writer now uses its own temporary file and renames it into place.

performance.attempt: Upload asks the remote about every object on each push so an interrupted upload completes; pushing only objects of new commits was the faster first version and left the remote without media.

entries.behavior: Exports one exact commit to a clean directory and reports drift from it: tracked files changed or deleted, shared links replaced, and files added outside declared outputs.

entries.behavior: The whole unit as committed, in 3 steps. 40e31b3 (added): Judges one unit: frozen size, complexity and dependencies, and performance only against a baseline with the identical unit, method and comparison context; otherwise incomplete or incompatible. 1d5f793 (<module>, budgetFindings, limited added, sizeFinding, unlimited added, unmeasured added): Complexity is a count only where decision points are counted: TypeScript, JavaScript and Svelte. A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. The measure and status commands, the history index, the component panel and the growth table show the value, the reason or the note. After 1d5f793 (<module>, budgetFindings, frozenFinding added, isFrozen added, sizeFinding removed, unlimited, verdict added): The size of what a unit emits is judged for each execution target against a limit of its own, whenever the unit is judged and not only when its source changed. An output the unit's baseline does not cover is a missing baseline with the detail no-limit-for-output, and one that was measured at the baseline and is gone is a missing measurement. sizeFinding became frozenFinding, which judges any frozen number under the name its limit has in the ledger.

entries.behavior: A verification follows the processes each check starts by their parent links, also one that left the group or session as a daemon does. One that is still running after the check ended, and after two seconds to end by itself, is stopped, and the check has failed with a failure of its own, whatever its exit code was. A process is signalled only when its id and start time are the ones that were seen. Before, such a check passed and its daemon ran on.

simplification.attempt: Finding the processes by a marker in their environment was considered and dropped: it would read the environment of every process. Asking only for the children of known processes needed one command per level of the tree; one read of ids, parents and start times per look replaced it. The runner grew.

performance.attempt: Measured on this machine with 737 processes: one read takes about 19 ms, taken every 200 ms while a check runs and once after it ends; a check that left something waits up to 2.5 s more. Looking only when the check ends was rejected: a parent that has exited no longer links to its daemon.

entries.behavior: Names the branches of code a repository knows. A local branch keeps its name and tip. A branch it has only as remote-tracking refs keeps its plain name when the remotes agree on its tip, so a clone rebuilds the index it was pushed from; a remote tip that differs from the local branch of that name, or from another remote, is listed beside it as <remote>:<branch>, which no local branch can be called because Git forbids the colon. Evidence, notes, archived source, tags and a remote's HEAD are never branches.

entries.behavior: Complexity is a count only where decision points are counted: TypeScript, JavaScript and Svelte. A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. The measure and status commands, the history index, the component panel and the growth table show the value, the reason or the note. After 1d5f793 (<module>, harnessBudget, limitOf added, noted added, unavailable removed, unreviewed added): A line says frozen at a number only where a reviewed limit is known for the revision: the baseline the record itself judged the value against, else the limit in the ledger of that revision. Without one it says that a freeze is declared and no reviewed limit is recorded there, where it used to say frozen for any measured value. A metric without a value keeps not frozen with its reason, a partial value keeps its note, and a value that exceeded its reviewed limit says what it grew from and to.

simplification.attempt: Until 1d5f793 (not improved): The rule is one function per kind of file and one more case in the judgement of a frozen metric. A declaration in every manifest was considered and dropped: the reviewed ledger already carries the decision. The code grew. After 1d5f793 (improved): One function decides the limit for the three shapes of a line, measured, unavailable and not measured, which removed the separate function for unavailable values; it was split into limitOf and unreviewed after lint measured complexity 11.

performance.attempt: Until 1d5f793 (not applicable): One lookup per owned file per measurement; not measured. After 1d5f793 (not applicable): Not applicable: a few comparisons per shown metric.

entries.behavior: The whole unit as committed, in 2 steps. f240fbd (added): Adds the console views over the history index: component map with search, focus, keyboard movement and a text list, comparison, recorded history, growth and earlier reports, each loading its data on demand and fitting a phone (its four views are two rows of two there), with the fixed synthetic history and the generated scale registry used to test them. 1d5f793 (<module>, harnessClient): The history index keeps one side per source tree: files, units, scenarios and the dependency graph. entries.behavior: The built servers of a browser run are started from a copy of the finished build that belongs to the run. A built server loads its files as they are asked for, so a rebuild of the checkout replaced what a running server had not loaded yet: a refused console page then answered 500 instead of 403, which an independent full check met while another check was building in the same checkout. The identity of the directory is taken before and after the copy and compared with the copy: a directory that holds no build, or one that another build is changing, stops the run with that reason.

A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. After 1d5f793 (<module>, BudgetService.failures, describe, subjectOf added, unfrozen added): A failure about an emitted size names its target: growth without approval, an output that is gone since its baseline, an output that became measurable, and an output the baseline of the unit does not cover each say what a reviewer must do. subjectOf words what a finding is about; unfrozen words the two cases of a number that has no limit although the unit has a baseline.

entries.behavior: The whole unit as committed, in 4 steps. 40e31b3 (added): Adds source-bound verification (143e486): a commit is exported to a clean snapshot, its affected checks run in their own process groups, captures are judged against each scenario contract, tracked files that change fail the snapshot, reasons and frozen budgets are gated, and the sealed record is stored whatever the outcome. Only a passing, intact record of an ancestor may narrow what reruns. f240fbd (RecordAssemblyService.assemble, snapshotFailures): Ties a capture to compiled files: declared builds are identified in the snapshot by a digest of every file, evidence may name a build, and a capture whose server reported another identity is rejected even when it carries the current revision. The reports server reports the digest of the files it was started from. 1d5f793 (<module>, RecordAssemblyService.assemble, RecordAssemblyService.reasons removed): The record names Harness itself and every declared tool with the version it reported in the snapshot, and the answer of the reasons gate is handed in, so it may be given step by step along the history. 1d5f793 (judgedScenarios added): A test file may declare a command of its own in harness.verify.json, and declared tools are asked for their version in the snapshot after setup: the record names Harness itself and each tool, and a tool that reports nothing fails the verification before any check runs. After 1d5f793 (<module>, RecordAssemblyService.budgeted): Unchanged units that a change reaches through a dependency are judged when they emit an output, not only when they have a performance budget: a build can grow with what it is built from while its own source stays as it is.

simplification.attempt: 40e31b3 (not applicable): The gates are judged in one assembly step from what the run observed. An earlier form that trusted the requested base was removed after review, which was a correction and not a simplification. f240fbd (improved): The stamp check was split into a revision part and a build part to stay under the complexity limit; a stamp file inside the build was considered and dropped because the digest alone needs no self-reference. 1d5f793 (improved): The assembly no longer loads reasons itself and lost that code; ordering the scenarios moved into a function to stay within the length limit. 1d5f793 (improved): The plan of one file check and the ordering of scenarios each moved into a function to stay within the complexity and length limits. After 1d5f793 (not applicable): None attempted beyond one more condition on the shared emittedTargets.

performance.attempt: 40e31b3 (not applicable): Not benchmarked. The cost is the checks themselves plus a comparison of the snapshot after setup and after every check. f240fbd (not applicable): Hashing the build directory runs twice per verification and once per server start; not measured. 1d5f793 (not applicable): Not measured. 1d5f793 (not applicable): One short command per declared tool per verification; not measured. After 1d5f793 (not improved): A verification whose change reaches emitting units measures those units too, one size lookup each. Not measured.

entries.behavior: The whole unit as committed, in 4 steps. 40e31b3 (added): Builds one revision's detail from what is stored for it: its registry graph, its attached records with resolved media and origin, and its reasons. f240fbd (<module>, RevisionDetailService.build, RevisionDetailService.constructor, RevisionDetailService.registry, comparison): The history index now states what every commit changed against its first parent, computed from the source of both commits by the impact service, and unit versions cover owned files; a history without records no longer shows an empty impact. 1d5f793 (<module>, RevisionDetailService.build): The history index keeps one side per source tree: files, units, scenarios and the dependency graph. A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. The measure and status commands, the history index, the component panel and the growth table show the value, the reason or the note.

entries.behavior: The whole unit as committed, in 3 steps. 40e31b3 (added): Reports measurements, limits and ledger history, and benchmarks a unit. 1d5f793 (budgetMeasure, budgetStatus): Complexity is a count only where decision points are counted: TypeScript, JavaScript and Svelte. A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. The measure and status commands, the history index, the component panel and the growth table show the value, the reason or the note. After 1d5f793 (budgetMeasure): harness budget measure gives each emitted size its execution target, so the rows of one unit can be told apart.

simplification.attempt: 40e31b3 (improved): Signing moved to its own workflow for the 220-line file limit. 1d5f793 (not improved): The rule is one function per kind of file and one more case in the judgement of a frozen metric. A declaration in every manifest was considered and dropped: the reviewed ledger already carries the decision. The code grew. After 1d5f793 (not applicable): None attempted: one more field.

performance.attempt: 40e31b3 (not applicable): No hot path: it runs once per command on small inputs. 1d5f793 (not applicable): One lookup per owned file per measurement; not measured. After 1d5f793 (not applicable): Not applicable.
